newsitem.title: UK: At least two berths shut at Novorossiisk oil port.
newsitem.headline: At least two berths shut at Novorossiisk oil port.

text.p: The main Russian Black Sea oil port of Novorossiisk was operating with only two berths on Thursday after an oil spill earlier this week forced three berths to close, shipping sources said.
The sources said the main number one berth was operating normally and berth number seven was also open. Berths two, three and six were expected to stay closed on Thursday.
But a shipping source said that while berths one and seven were officially open, one vessel had refused to dock at berth seven fearing the risk of fire from the spill.
Nearly 400 tonnes of oil spilled at a terminal in Novorossiisk when a pipeline burst open on Tuesday night, the Russian Emergencies Ministry said on Wednesday.
A spokesman said that about 13 tonnes had spilled into the sea but the port was operating.

"Berths two and six are currently closed due to the pollution. Berths one and seven are officially open but one vessel did refuse to dock. We don't know when berth two is going to reopen," the source said.
Seven crude oil tankers and three fuel oil tankers were expected to arrive over the next three days.
The other Black Sea port of Odessa was operating normally.
